key_insight: Tensor-network decomposition turns a high-dimensional quantum dynamics problem into independent lower-dimensional propagations that can run asynchronously across distributed quantum and classical hardware.
engineering_relevance: The work offers a practical route to hybrid quantum simulation workflows by mapping entangled evolutions onto parallel tasks and compiling them efficiently for hardware with native partial-entangling gates.
method: Represent the multidimensional time-evolution operator as a tensor network.
Lift the problem into an elevated Hilbert space where dynamics split into independent subproblems.
Implement distributed circuits on trapped-ion hardware using native $XX(\theta)$ gates.
evidence_signal: In a vibrational spectroscopy demonstration on a protonated water cluster, the quantum results agreed with classical results to within 4 cm$^{-1}$, while the gate compilation reduced expected two-qubit gate infidelity by more than 30%.
watch_item: The approach depends on tensor-network structure and hardware-specific compilation, so performance and scalability may degrade for systems that are less amenable to low-rank decompositions or native partial-entangling gates.
paper_title: Tensor-Network-Based Distributed Quantum Dynamics on Independent Quantum Computers
